title: Soccer Calibration Pack
headline_insight: On this international-soccer corpus the market is sharper than the model: model Brier is 0.227887 versus market 0.142726 over 9,003 rows, and the gap is widest exactly where the two disagree most.
what_it_means: When model and market diverge by 0.10 or more (n=4406), the model is the closer forecast only 21.52% of the time. Late-game calibration also drifts, with expected calibration error climbing to 0.4978 in the 75-91 minute bucket. This is a published null, not a win.
how_to_read: The Murphy decomposition splits Brier into reliability and resolution; the disagreement buckets show who is closer when model and market pull apart; the minute buckets show calibration error over the clock.
why_it_matters: It is honest market-efficiency evidence, the model does not beat the market here, reported as-is rather than hidden.
caveat: The soccer_intl corpus is only 9,003 rows, far smaller than MLB or NBA, so confidence intervals are wide and single-fold reads are not durable.
as_of: n=9003 soccer_intl corpus (no generation timestamp in artifact)
